title: Task, async, await, and ValueTask
hook: async is not a runtime daemon. The C# compiler rewrites your method into a state machine that parks on await and resumes when a Task or ValueTask completes.

sections.heading: The compiler’s state machine
sections.prose: An async method returns quickly with a Task (or ValueTask) that represents the rest of the method. At each await, if the awaited awaitable is already completed, execution continues synchronously — a cache hit path. If not, the state machine captures locals, hooks a continuation, and returns. When the I/O completes, the continuation runs the next state. That is why you can write linear code for Redis then HTTP then a RabbitMQ publish. Locals that look like stack variables may live on a heap-allocated state-machine box for the duration of the awaits. Naming methods with the Async suffix is convention, not a compiler rule; the compiler only cares about the async modifier and the return type: void, Task, Task<T>, ValueTask, or ValueTask<T>.

snippets.label: Hot cache path with ValueTask
snippets.explanation: A memory hit completes without allocating a Task. A Redis miss still awaits. Callers must await the ValueTask at most once.

sections.heading: Task versus ValueTask in .NET 10
sections.prose: Task is a reference type with a rich API: WhenAll, WhenAny, ContinueWith (prefer await), and exception aggregation. It is the default return type for public APIs. ValueTask is a struct that can hold a result, a Task, or an IValueTaskSource used by pooled pipes and sockets. Use ValueTask when a profiler shows Task allocations on a path that usually finishes synchronously. Never store a ValueTask to await it later twice; the underlying source may have been reused. If you need to pass the operation to WhenAll, call .AsTask() once. async Task still allocates a Task on every slow path; that is normal and cheaper than blocking a thread.

interviewTakeaways: await is a compiler transformation, not a new thread.
ValueTask is an allocation optimization for completed-sync paths; await it once.
Public surface area should usually return Task unless you have measured otherwise.
commonPitfalls: Awaiting the same ValueTask instance twice after a cache miss that used IValueTaskSource.
Using async on a method that never awaits — the compiler warns, and you still pay a state machine.
Confusing Task.Run (queue CPU work) with async (compose waits).

jsTsCorrelations.concept: async functions always return a Promise
jsTsCorrelations.note: A JS async function boxes a Promise even on a sync return. C# can return ValueTask to skip a heap object on the sync path; JS has no equivalent struct awaitable.
